schemes.description: Credit-bearing taught modules in which a supervisor leads a student team drawn from different disciplines and levels of study that contributes to an ongoing research project addressing genuine research questions; students may stay with a project across semesters. Projects are academic-led; external involvement varies by project (e.g. St Andrews Forest VIP joins academics, practitioners and local 'neighbours' and produces a commissioned report and group presentation for the University's Environmental Sustainability Board, i.e. an internal client).
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Not re-verified in this review (legacy row states Arts and Science students at different study levels)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: One VIP per semester; must be taken for credit; application required (rolling, projects may close when full). Faculty-level eligibility not re-verified.
schemes.credit_assessment: 10, 15, 20 or 30 SCOTCAT credits per semester; 5 credits for returning students; appears on transcript
schemes.project_evidence: Team contributes to an ongoing research project addressing 'genuine research questions' [2][3]; St Andrews Forest example produces a commissioned report and group presentation [4].
schemes.group_evidence: 'A VIP brings together a student team formed from different disciplines and levels of study' [3]; the team addresses research questions jointly [2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Projects are academic research projects led by a supervisor [3]. No VIP-wide evidence of external organisations setting briefs or receiving outputs. The St Andrews Forest VIP involves 'practitioners and our neighbours', but its report is commissioned by the University's Environmental Sustainability Board (internal) [4]. No list of VIPs naming external companies or charities was found. WebFetch of the VIP projects page (2026-10-13): 19-21 projects listed (e.g. Mutual Aid Clinic, Beauty and the Biz, PeaceHub, Biodiversity Literacy) and 'None of the projects names an external partner organisation, company, or charity'; the page states no faculty eligibility.
schemes.partner_role: Mostly internal academic research; occasional external practitioners/community participants in individual projects
schemes.deliverable: Research contributions; project-specific outputs (e.g. report and group presentation in St Andrews Forest VIP)
schemes.unresolved: Faculty eligibility not stated on projects page (legacy row says Arts and Science); the page does not name external partners, so C stays Unclear.

Outputs include research reports, videos, educational resources used at the University, creative work or websites.

profile_md:
**St Andrews** (reduced-depth review, six areas queried): no scheme was verified that meets all three criteria with a documented external client and current delivery.

- **VIP:** credit-bearing mixed-discipline research teams (applications for 2026/27 confirmed). Fetching the projects page shows 19 projects, none naming an external partner, so C is Unclear. Faculty eligibility is not stated (legacy row says Arts and Science).
- **STEP:** online 7-week team consulting projects in 2026, but the clients are University Schools and units (internal, C = No).
- **CS3099:** year-3 team software project with Experian and Skyscanner involvement reported in 2025, role unspecified.
- **Management MSc:** advertises consultancy projects with local organisations, but no corresponding compulsory module or group structure was found.
- **Playfair:** student-run pro bono consultancy with teams of 5-6 and external clients, but evidence is secondary and undated and it is not a University scheme.

Science, humanities/social science, Medicine, Divinity and Law yielded no external-client team routes. Provision is isolated and mostly internal or research-led.
gaps: Further departmental instances may exist but were not found in reduced-depth search. Open items: VIP faculty eligibility and external partners per project; CS3099 partner role and whether compulsory; the Management MSc module behind 'consultancy projects'; Playfair current status and eligibility; ScotGEM Agents of Change group/partner role; Law and Divinity only lightly searched (one combined query); one query per area only.
